questions.stem: What does the xylem transport, and from where to where?

options.text: Water and dissolved ions, upward from the roots
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Sucrose is the phloem's cargo.

options.text: Oxygen from the leaves to the roots
options.explanation: Oxygen diffuses; xylem sap is water and ions.
Amino acids ride the phloem in either direction.

questions.stem: What fills a mature xylem vessel?

options.explanation: Starch sits in storage tissue, not xylem.

options.text: A hollow tube of dead cells with no cell contents
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Mature xylem cells are dead and empty.
That describes phloem architecture.

questions.stem: Which material reinforces the xylem walls?

options.explanation: Chitin builds fungal and insect structures, not plant vessels.
Keratin is an animal protein.
Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Cellulose is general wall material; the reinforcement named here is lignin.

questions.stem: Which substances travel in the phloem?

options.explanation: Those ride the xylem.
Gases move by diffusion, not phloem transport.
Both are insoluble storage and structural materials.
Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

questions.stem: Why does sucrose made in the leaves travel to other parts of the plant?

options.text: It is produced where photosynthesis runs and needed where growth or storage happens
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
Leaves can store briefly; transport matches supply to demand.
Phloem flow is not gravity-driven.
The two systems simply carry different cargoes.

questions.stem: State the roles of xylem and phloem in one sentence each.
questions.modelAnswer: Xylem lifts water and dissolved mineral ions from root to shoot; phloem ships sucrose and amino acids from their source to wherever the plant needs them.

questions.stem: Describe the structure of the phloem.
questions.modelAnswer: Living cells join into tubes whose small sieve holes let substances pass.

questions.stem: Explain why lignin reinforcement suits the xylem's function.
questions.modelAnswer: The upward water column places the vessels under tension, and strong lignin-thickened walls stop them collapsing while letting the hollow bore stay open for flow.

questions.stem: A ring of bark is removed from a trunk, cutting the phloem but leaving the xylem intact. Predict the effect.
questions.modelAnswer: The xylem keeps water rising, so leaves stay supplied, but sugars can no longer pass the ring, so stores and roots below it starve while swellings form above the cut.
